reasons: Detection is correct: Section 14.3 selects California law (an accepted fallback) but mandates binding single-arbitrator AAA arbitration in San Francisco, so the dispute forum deviates from the playbook's court-adjudication requirement; medium severity is right because the seat is domestic, not a foreign arbitration (walk-away).

The redline reaches the playbook position: it strikes the arbitration mechanics (AAA rules, single arbitrator, entry-of-judgment sentence) and substitutes exclusive jurisdiction and venue in the state and federal courts of San Francisco County, while leaving the governing-law sentence (California, conflicts and CISG carve-outs) untouched.

Retaining California law rather than forcing New York is defensible under the rule (California is an express fallback) and is the smaller edit; the comment transparently discloses that we took the fallback instead of the preferred New York position.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (ratio 0.648) is explained by the rule itself: removing a mandatory arbitration regime necessarily rewrites the dispute-resolution sentences, and no unrelated terms were altered. Deleting the AAA fee-allocation clause is a proper consequential cleanup, and each party's own-cost sentence is preserved.
Comment is accurate, concise, in first person plural, correctly prefixed, and cites the playbook basis and fallback rationale without lecturing.
Minor, non-blocking cleanup: the section heading still reads 'Choice of Law; Arbitration; Venue' even though arbitration has been removed \u2014 consider conforming it to 'Choice of Law; Venue'.
